newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Sun Hung Kai Prop posts 21 pct rise in interim net.
newsitem.headline: Sun Hung Kai Prop posts 21 pct rise in interim net.

text.p: Hong Kong property developer Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd posted a 21 percent rise in interim net profit on Thursday and said it expects "considerable growth" for its full-year results.
The company said net profit rose to HK$6.25 billion in the six months to December 31, 1996, compared with HK$5.15 billion in the same period the previous year.
Turnover rose to HK$14.88 billion compared with HK$12.64 billion.

"Most residential properties scheduled for completion in the current financial year have been presold. With a buoyant property market, the group's results for the current year are expected to show considerable growth," chairman and chief executive Walter Kwok said in a statement.
Analysts praised the interim results and said they were optimistic about the company's outlook.
"An exceptional set of results," said David Low, property analyst at Asia Equity.

Sun Hung Kai Properties said property sales jumped to HK$8.1 billion during the half-year from HK$1.97 billion in the same period of 1995. Major projects sold included the King's Park Villa development in Kowloon and Villa Tiara in Tuen Muen.
The group was one of the chief beneficiaries of the upswing in Hong Kong's residential property market in 1996.
It reaped gains from both higher sales volume and a 30 percent rise in residential property prices in 1996, analysts said.
But they added the increase came on the back of a low base.
"In financial year 1996, the group had completed a lot of industrial properties which were not received well by the market," said Edward Chan, head of research at Amsteel Securities.
The company retained these as rental properties, he said.
Sun Hung Kai Properties said its investment properties were practically fully let and its industrial buildings were almost fully let.
Recurrent earnings are likely to have risen by 15 percent, boosted by the inclusion of new properties in the portfolio as well as a small increase in average rental rates, said Low.
"The Royal Garden and Royal Park hotels both achieved very satisfactory results during the period, with occupancy rates reaching 97 percent and 95 percent respectively," the company said.
The property developer said it expected to complete 2.6 million square feet of properties in the second half of this financial year compared with 2.3 million in the first half.
Presales of its East Point City development in Tseung Kwan O and its Villa Tiara project in Tuen Mun would be completed in the second half, it added.
"Almost all residential units in both developments have already been sold," it said.
Amsteel's Chan said he expected 20 percent growth to HK$13.2 billion for the full year while Asia Equity's Low said he was likely to make a slight downward revision to his forecast of 35 percent.
